newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen sideways, small caps rule.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen sideways, small caps rule.

text.p: Singapore shares were seen trading sideways on Friday with activity concentrated on small cap stocks, recent listings and electronics counters, dealers said.
"The big funds aren't buying. Small caps are where the action is," said one dealer at a local brokerage.
On Thursday the Straits Times Industrials Index closed almost unchanged, up a bare 0.73 point to 1,967.14.
Dealers said the market faced more downward pressure than upside impetus in the near term as worries of a fall in the property market combined with fallout from regional currency instability.
"Domestically and regionally we're not looking at a very positive situation," one dealer said.
